title: Canonical cubical structure on a rigidified line
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $p:G\to S$ a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with geometrically connected fibres and identity $e$. The group operations satisfy the commutative group identities, and separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume either (a) $p$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], so that $G$ is an abelian scheme, or (b) $S$ is normal (all local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]) and every geometric fibre is semiabelian: over an algebraically closed residue-field extension $k$ it is an extension, exact as fppf sheaves, $1\to(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\to G_k\to A_k\to1$, with $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$, and $A_k$ a proper smooth geometrically connected $k$-group scheme. For every invertible module $L$ on $G$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and every rigidification $r:e^*L\simeq\mathcal O_S$ (tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]), there is exactly one cubical structure compatible with $r$ [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line]. Every rigidification-preserving isomorphism between such lines preserves their cubical structures. These structures commute with restriction of the base and with pullback by group-scheme homomorphisms whenever both groups satisfy (a) or (b).

proof.text: Form $C=\Theta_3(L)$ as in [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line]. Inserting $e$ in coordinate $i$ pairs each factor $m_I^*L$ not involving $i$ with the inverse factor indexed by $I\cup\{i\}$; evaluate $e^*L$ with $r$. Evaluation of a line against its dual gives a canonical face trivialization $c_i$ of $C$. On intersections the same pairings give the same section: locally their coefficient is the product of the same units and their inverses. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-picard-cube-face-detection] with all three factors equal to $G$, $M=C$. Its proper alternative holds in (a), and its normal semiabelian alternative holds in (b). It gives a nowhere vanishing section $t$ of $C$, initially with no normalization.

proof.text:
Write $f_i=j_i^*t/c_i$, a unit on the face $x_i=e$. Their restrictions to face intersections agree. Denote the common restriction to $x_i=x_j=e$ by $f_{ij}$, and to the all-identity section by $f_{123}$. Regard each of these functions on $G^3$ by forgetting the coordinates set equal to $e$. Define
$$\tau=t\,f_1^{-1}f_2^{-1}f_3^{-1}f_{12}f_{13}f_{23}f_{123}^{-1}.$$
For example, on $x_1=e$ the scalar factor multiplying $c_1$ is
$$f_1 f_1^{-1}f_{12}^{-1}f_{13}^{-1}f_{12}f_{13}f_{123}f_{123}^{-1}=1.$$
The other two substitutions give the same cancellation. Thus $\tau$ is nowhere vanishing and has exactly the three required face restrictions.

proof.text: We will use [lem-sfb-relative-group-unit-axis-factorization] on $G^3$ and $G^4$. Its proper alternative applies in (a). In (b) normality implies reducedness: each local ring is a domain and hence has no nonzero nilpotents. If $\tau'$ is another nowhere vanishing cube section with the prescribed face restrictions, its quotient $u=\tau'/\tau$ is a unit on $G^3$ equal to $1$ on each identity face, and hence on each identity axis. The cited factorization gives $u=1$. This proves uniqueness even before symmetry and the cocycle condition are imposed.

proof.text:
A permutation of the coordinates permutes the factors of $\Theta_3(L)$ and the canonical face sections $c_i$. The permuted $\tau$ therefore has the same face restrictions as $\tau$, so the uniqueness just proved makes it equal to $\tau$. For the cocycle, expand the four copies of $\Theta_3(L)$ in the displayed identity of [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line] and cancel the factors indexed by equal sums. The quotient
$$v=\frac{\tau(x,y,z)\tau(x+y,w,z)}{\tau(y,w,z)\tau(x,y+w,z)}$$
is consequently a unit on $G^4$. On each of its four identity axes every displayed triple has at least one identity coordinate, so all four sections evaluate to their canonical unit sections; thus each axis restriction of $v$ is $1$. The factorization of [lem-sfb-relative-group-unit-axis-factorization] for $n=4$ gives $v=1$. This proves the cocycle condition and hence existence of a compatible cubical structure.

proof.text: For a rigidification-preserving isomorphism $\alpha:L\simeq L'$, the tensor product of its eight pullbacks sends $\Theta_3(L)$ to $\Theta_3(L')$. The cancellation on every identity face commutes with $\alpha$ because $\alpha$ preserves $r$. Thus $\Theta_3(\alpha)(\tau_L)$ and $\tau_{L'}$ have the same face restrictions; their quotient is $1$ by step 3. Therefore every such isomorphism preserves the cube sections.

proof.text: Pullback along a base restriction, or a group-scheme homomorphism, carries every partial-sum map in $\Theta_3$ to the corresponding partial-sum map and carries $e$ to $e$. Tensor inverse image preserves the evaluation pairings of a line and its dual (locally this is multiplication of a unit and its inverse). It therefore carries the face normalization, permutation equality and cocycle equality of $\tau$ to the same equalities for the pulled-back line. Whenever the new group satisfies (a) or (b), its unique structure from steps 1--4 must equal this pulled-back structure. This proves the stated compatibilities, including identity and iterated pullbacks.
